'I'm not really into politics'
Being Unbothered by Politics Is a Privilege — One Many Can’t Afford.
Seun Unfiltered
Mar 29, 2025

I've always been an opinionated person for as long as I can remember. Having lived in both the UK and Nigeria, I’ve been exposed to vastly different political climates—both of which have shaped my understanding of injustice.

These experiences essentially ‘radicalised’ me against systemic inequalities. So, when I discuss political topics or human rights issues and someone responds with, “I’m not really into politics,” it forces me to reconsider how they engage with the world.

When you move from relying on a petrol generator because government electricity is unreliable to having access to 24/7 electricity, you begin to grasp how deeply unfair the world is. You realise just how much the Global North benefits from the hardships endured by the Global South. I first understood this when I was six, and those thoughts have never left me.

Politics isn’t a trend, like clothes or shoes. It shapes our lives, whether we acknowledge it or not.

I want to clarify that I’m not saying everyone needs to be a political fanatic. That’s not the issue at hand. The problem is choosing to remain unaware of the world around you—wilful ignorance—while simultaneously complaining about everything. Politics affects our livelihoods, our health, and every aspect of our existence.

When someone says, “I’m not really into politics,” it usually reveals one of two things: either they are uninformed, or they are speaking from a place of privilege. Ignorance may be bliss, but it’s a privilege many cannot afford. To live unaffected by political changes and global injustices is a luxury.

For me, witnessing injustices has fuelled a deep anger—one that only grew the more I educated myself. I’ve channelled that energy into activism and my work with charities. But at the very least, I believe that awareness should be the baseline. As James Baldwin once wrote, “You think your pain and your heartbreak are unprecedented in the history of the world, but then you read.”

Your ignorance will not save you. Sitting on the fence when it comes to human rights issues will not protect you. Just because you haven't lived through war or genocide doesn’t mean it cannot happen to you.

Many in the West believe that their geographical location insulates them from calamities, but reality paints a different picture. The cost of living is at an all-time high. Food poverty is rising to unprecedented levels. We are on the verge of an economic depression.

The UK government is preparing to cut disability benefits for millions while the rich continue to get richer. And yet, some people still believe politics doesn’t affect them?

Only through political consciousness can we begin to address the very issues we complain about. Change happens when we engage with facts rather than relying solely on emotion.

If we want to challenge the political class, we must first understand the policies and systems that govern our lives. Too often, we blame each other for society’s problems instead of recognising the role of those in power who create and enforce these policies.

History shows that even under military rule and dictatorship, people still went to the cinema and lived their lives. Many assume we would recognise censorship if it happened to us, yet we ignore warning signs like the TikTok ban in the U.S.—a clear attempt to control the spread of uncensored information. We underestimate the importance of educating ourselves.

So, if you say you’re “not really into politics,” ask yourself: how much do you really know about your world? How does politics shape your life? If you can’t answer these questions, it’s time to pick up a book, listen to the news—hell, even scroll through TikTok. It’s time to be conscious.

Being Unbothered by Politics Is a Privilege—One Many Can’t Afford.
